long_biography.plain_text:
Ferro began operating a roof-sealant business while still in high school and continued it through college. After selling that company and running a division of its acquirer, he founded Click Commerce in 1994, built internet-based supply-chain software and took the company public. Its eventual sale supplied the capital for his next phase.

Through Merrick Ventures, Ferro shifted from operator to technology investor, backing and chairing medical-imaging company Merge Healthcare before its acquisition by IBM. He also founded Higi, developed healthcare-imaging patents and moved into newspaper ownership through the Chicago Sun-Times and Tribune Publishing. Media became a prominent but finite chapter; his continuing platform is Merrick, focused on technology, healthcare data and artificial intelligence.
